facts.claim: Go1 is the largest online learning library in the world.
Go1 is built for people-first L&D leaders.
Go1's platform is designed to deliver 'all your team's learning needs, one easy platform'.
Go1 differentiates itself by offering a vast course variety (80,000+ courses from 250+ providers) compared to single-source providers with a narrow focus.
Go1 emphasizes global coverage with ready-to-deploy content in 40+ languages.
Go1 positions itself as more than a content aggregator by delivering more value across key features like usability and integration.
Go1's value proposition includes agility and content benefits for L&D solutions.
Go1's platform is designed to meet organizational and end-user goals by providing the depth, range, and variety of learning content needed.
Go1 integrates learning into everyday work through its intelligent agent, Morgan.
Go1's core promise is to simplify employee training with an AI-powered L&D solution.
Someone completes a Go1 course or learning resource almost three times every second, demonstrating massive scale and usage.

Go1 has developed this Code of Conduct (the “**Code**”) so our Board members, officers, employees, contractors, partners, and suppliers of any goods or services to Go1 (collectively “**you**” or “**your**”) clearly understand the kind of behaviour and conduct we expect to stay true to our values, achieve our goals, and make decisions in a legal, ethical, and considered way.

As a truly global business, Go1 is subject to a huge variety of laws such as those related to governance, data privacy, security, compliance, and employment. Alongside our other policies, the Code is intended to help you navigate applicable laws and regulations whilst working with Go1. Although our policies typically exceed Go1’s legal requirements, there may be times when local laws, regulations, customs, or business practices differ from the policies and procedures provided to you. If this occurs, please comply with your region’s laws and regulations, and ensure you seek further guidance before conforming to local customs or business practices. The consequences of engaging in offending conduct may include reputational damage to you or Go1, termination of your employment or business relationship with Go1, fines, and civil or criminal charges.

Go1 vs other learning platforms: Compare core features
------------------------------------------------------

Choosing a learning solution isn’t about picking winners and losers—it’s about finding the best fit. We respect what others like LinkedIn Learning and OpenSesame bring to the table, but we also know where Go1 goes further. Explore how we deliver more value across key features.

| **Feature/Capability** | **Go1** | **Content aggregators** | Single-source providers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Course variety** | 80,000+ courses from 250+ providers | Coverage varies depending on region and provider availability | Narrow focus with limited formats and variety |
| **Language availability** | Ready-to-deploy in 40+ languages with global coverage | Coverage varies depending on topic | Limited to a narrow set of languages and dialects |
| **Usability (Admin Experience)** | AI-powered tools for discovery, curation, and reporting | Manual, time-consuming workflows and basic search | Fragmented admin view across multiple platforms |
| **Usability (Learner Experience)** | Personalized homepages and recommendations for every learner | Same static view for everyone | Different look and feel with each provider |
| **Integrations** | 70+ integrations with leading LMS, LXP, HRIS, and productivity tools | Basic integrations with limited subset of partners | Learners redirected outside their core systems, reducing engagement |
| **Pricing** | Simple, transparent subscription pricing | New features or content often come with hidden costs.

Go1 helps organizations address falling engagement and completion scores by providing a new approach to upskilling, reskilling, and retaining employees.
Go1 supports leadership and learning development for staff across multiple campuses in educational institutions.
Go1 enables organizations to build a learning and development (L&D) team from scratch, increasing active learners, boosting engagement, developing leaders, and ensuring compliance.
Go1's AI-powered L&D solution includes an intelligent agent named Morgan that brings learning into everyday work.
Go1 can be used to move compliance training closer to the point of need, delivering it when employees encounter relevant situations rather than front-loading it.
Go1 supports micro-learning by breaking longer courses into 5-10 minute segments that employees can complete between meetings.
Go1 allows leveraging internal expertise to create relevant training by enabling top performers to share skills and real examples.
Go1 provides instant access to over 100,000 learning resources from top content providers through its Go1 Premium catalogue.
Go1's learning resources are sourced, aggregated, and curated to help organizations stay compliant and maintain high performance.
Go1 learning can be accessed within an organization's existing learning ecosystem or directly via the Go1 platform (MyGo1 or Go1 Learn).
Go1 integrates with the Go1 API for extended functionality and customization.

**What to do:**Move training closer to the point of need. For example, instead of front-loading all [compliance training](https://www.go1.com/solutions/category/compliance) in week one, deliver it when employees actually encounter those situations and offer skill-building courses right before project launches or role changes.

**What to do:** Leverage [micro-learning](https://www.go1.com/podcast/s2e2-craig-mcfadyen) by breaking longer courses into 5-10 minute segments that employees can complete between meetings. Each segment should cover one specific concept or skill.

Using[internal expertise](https://www.go1.com/blog/leveraging-internal-expertise-for-better-learning-and-development-programs) addresses one of training's biggest challenges: relevance. Your top performers know exactly which skills matter most and can share real examples of how they've applied them successfully.

raw_passages.text: [Meet Morgan - Go1’s intelligent agent that brings learning into everyday work](https://www.go1.com/product/morgan)
![Image 1: Go1 Employee Training](https://images.prismic.io/go1-com/aSZhQmGnmrmGqVTR_9-6-.avif?auto=format%2Ccompress&fit=max&w=3840)

The Go1 Content Hub is the largest curated eLearning library from the world’s top training providers, available for a single subscription within your existing learning platform, or available on ours. There's even an opportunity to upgrade the Go1 Platform for Enterprise. With Go1, you’ll always have the right training courses to upskill, re-train, and retain your employees.

If you have an existing platform to deliver learning, the Go1 Content Hub seamlessly plugs in to hundreds of LMSs, HRISs, and Apps at the touch of a button. If you’re still seeking the right platform to deliver your learning, the Go1 Platform is available as a standalone SCORM-compliant solution.
*   [**Resources**](https://elearningindustry.com/directory/elearning-software/go1#)[**Resources**](https://elearningindustry.com/directory/elearning-software/go1#)
*   [**Software & Services**](https://elearningindustry.com/directory/elearning-software/go1#)[**Software & Services**](https://elearningindustry.com/directory/elearning-software/go1#)

As a leading EdTech company, Go1's mission is to unlock positive potential through a love for learning. Go1 is the world's most comprehensive digital learning aggregator, trusted by thousands of organizations to solve the challenge of curating content for diverse training and development needs. The depth and breadth of Go1's Content Hub enables organizations to create an enterprise content library and provide specific learning opportunities to meet any business need.

Content aggregation refers to the process of collecting a variety of different digital learning providers and making them available in one convenient, centralized location. A content aggregation model like Go1's means all your learning needs are catered for in a single subscription, so you don't have to compromise on the quality or quantity of what gets delivered.

Delivering on the Promise of Digital Learning With **Go1**
==========================================================
![Image 44: Go1 Hero-Shape](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67e5b0da600dc9b00112eac4/68a4bce66fbcfc085b99df30_Go1_Hero-Shape.avif)

Premium Pro offers e-learning content sourced from over 250 content providers (including Go1's expanded Pro Library) and accessed via the Go1 platform and/or third-party integrations. The content library includes pre-curated learning pathways and on-demand search capabilities enabling admins and learners to discover relevant content based on specific terms, topics, and providers. Premium Pro customers also have the option to provide learners with access to Blinkist Enterprise.

Our Compliance Bundle offers compliance-related e-learning content accessed via the Go1 platform and/or third-party integrations. Compliance Bundles include 20 e-learning courses that are pre-selected by Go1 and cover a broad range of compliance topics.

Essentials Select provides access to the Go1 Premium Essentials library, offering flexible course selection tailored to each organization’s needs. Depending on the selected plan, customers can activate and use either 10, 25, or 50 courses at any given time, accessible through the Go1 platform or third-party integrations. Essentials Select admins can add Licensed Users to the account, assign specific e-learning courses, and monitor learning progress through reporting available on the Go1 platform (where applicable).

Licensed User: is a single identified user on a named user basis, who is authorized by you to access Go1 e-learning content. The number of individual users accessing Go1 e-learning content under your Agreement may not exceed the number of Licensed Users set out in the Order Form (“Service Capacity”).
To see what’s new, [visit our product page.](https://www.go1.com/go1-ai-launch)

That’s why we built **Go1 AI**: a new suite of features designed to simplify your workflow, save time, and bring more precision to your content decisions. Whether you’re building compliance programs, leadership tracks, or regional training plans, Go1 AI helps you find the right content faster and build more personalized learning journeys—without the manual lift.

Traditional keyword search tools can miss the mark. With **AI-enhanced search**, Go1 AI understands the intent behind your queries—suggesting contextually relevant content and skills in seconds, not hours. It maps your needs to Go1’s extensive content library with deeper relevance and fewer clicks.
![Image 1: Go1 AI Chat](https://images.prismic.io/go1-com/aB4BgSdWJ-7kR1Oc_261900db-b6e1-483f-af39-b5d3f8d77427_AI%2BChat.avif?auto=format,compress)

Sourced, aggregated, and curated to help you stay compliant and at the top of your game, your learning is available in your organization's existing learning ecosystem or directly via the Go1 platform (MyGo1 or Go1 Learn)
Go1 gives you instant access to more than 100,000 learning resources from the world’s best content providers through the Go1 Premium catalogue.

[Integrate with the Go1 API](https://help.go1.com/en/articles/4642648-integrate-with-the-go1-api)[Go1 Learn: Your Complete Admin Guide](https://help.go1.com/en/articles/11051747-go1-learn-your-complete-admin-guide)[Go1 Learn: Manager guide](https://help.go1.com/en/articles/13340890-go1-learn-manager-guide)[How to change my password (Go1 Learn)](https://help.go1.com/en/articles/13605031-how-to-change-my-password-go1-learn)

If your organization has Go1 - congratulations! You now have access to a world of digital learning to support your compliance needs, nurture your well-being, and empower your professional development.
[Meet Morgan - Go1’s intelligent agent that brings learning into everyday work](https://www.go1.com/product/morgan)
Since Go1's creation in 2015, we've grown into the largest online learning library in the world, built for people-first L&D leaders.
![Image 2](https://go1-com.cdn.prismic.io/go1-com/aNM7a55xUNkB1Cct_OnlineCourseProviders_Leader_Leader.svg?fit=max&w=256)
![Image 3](https://go1-com.cdn.prismic.io/go1-com/aNM8JJ5xUNkB1Cc3_SoftwareAdvice_frontrunners.svg?fit=max&w=1920)

Go1 Learn is our redesigned learning platform that makes content discovery and compliance training more intuitive, personalized, and engaging. Built with both learners and admins in mind, Go1 Learn replaces MyGo1 with a modern experience that drives meaningful learning outcomes for your organization.

Yes, admins and managers will have the ability to switch between MyGo1 and Go1 Learn until all the core functionality you need is available in Go1 Learn. This gives you time to become familiar with Go1 Learn while still accessing MyGo1 for functions that haven't yet been migrated.

Group management functionality will be available in Go1 Learn in[2026](https://www.go1.com/learn-roadmap).Until then, you can continue to use MyGo1 for group management while leveraging Go1 Learn for other admin tasks.

Learning assignment capabilities will be available in Go1 Learn in [early 2026](https://www.go1.com/learn-roadmap). Until this functionality is available, you can continue to use MyGo1 for learning assignments.

*   **Access to Go1 Learning**: Employees have access to a range of relevant development content through [Go1](https://www.go1.com/plans), with learning budgets to spend on what matters to them.
*   **Dedicated Learning Days**: Twice a year, the entire company steps away from day-to-day work to focus purely on learning, whether in teams or individually.
*   **Wellbeing Days**: You can’t learn (and work) effectively if you’re burned out. Two annual wellbeing days (on top of paid holiday) help employees recharge, and know that even our executives are taking the day.
*   **Structured Growth Conversations**: Three times a year, employees have dedicated check-ins to reflect on progress and map out their next steps—because growth shouldn’t be left to chance.

Hybrid work has changed the game, making it harder—but even more essential—to build a strong learning culture. The right approach is so important to keep employees engaged; it fuels innovation, retention, and long-term growth. In our latest episode of our L&D in 20 podcast, it was the Dan duo, as our host Dan Haywood sat down with our very own Dan MacPhail, Go1’s Director of Organizational Capability. Dan M. shared his take on closing the gaps left by fewer informal workplace interactions, challenges and opportunities of hybrid work, and how organizations can build a learning culture that thrives.

Go1 moved to a remote-first approach in February 2024. With team members across over 25 countries and some office sites still in place, we’ve figured out what works (and what doesn’t) for a global remote team. Here’s how we’ve built a thriving learning culture—and how you can do the same.
[Meet Morgan - Go1’s intelligent agent that brings learning into everyday work](https://www.go1.com/product/morgan)

[Start Personalized Free Trial](https://www.go1.com/small-business-lms#form)
![Image 7](https://images.prismic.io/go1-com/aYVnMt0YXLCxVe3P_Go1-for-SMBs.png?auto=format%2Ccompress&fit=max&w=1920)

Yes, Go1 has over 80,000 courses available spanning a wide variety of topics, languages, skills, industries, and formats. Go1’s full content library is available to customers who buy our Essentials Select plans. The only providers not included in these plans are premium providers: Blinkist, Coursera, Skillsoft, and Pluralsight.

Yes, the Go1 platform offers most of the same functionality as a standard LMS. You will be able to manage users, curate and assign content, and report on learning outcomes all within the Go1 platform. Learn more about our platform [here](https://www.go1.com/product/product-experience).

“Companies are embracing the opportunity to programmatically upskill, reskill and empower their workforces, and Go1 has emerged as the go-to provider of learning content to make that opportunity a reality,” said Craig Blair, Founder at AirTree Ventures. “We’re delighted to be a part of Go1’s global journey in building an enduring company at the helm of the Learning & Development ecosystem.”

“Go1 has built a platform that serves the needs of both employers looking to retain and upskill their talent and employees seeking training for their professional and personal development,” said S.Somasegar, Managing Director, Madrona. “Go1’s successful expansion into the US and other global markets means they not only serve global corporations but are uniquely suited for the far flung remote workforces of the next decade. We are excited to work with the team on the next phase of growth.”

“Leading organizations are recognizing the acute need to future-proof their workforces by providing comprehensive learning and development opportunities,” said Andrew Barnes, CEO of Go1. “The incredible team at Go1 has made huge strides in expanding our capabilities and offerings to ensure users have access to education that supports their growth. These recent investments allow Go1 to build on that momentum to explore new content and resources, enabling our platform to meet the needs of every organization and employee, and brings us closer to our goal of supporting one billion learners globally.”

●**Antony Ugoni, Chief Data Officer.** Ugoni has held a variety of senior leadership positions in data and analytics and is currently Chairperson on the advisory board for the Institute of Analytics Professionals of Australia. Ugoni will lead Go1’s data and data science teams, serving both internal business intelligence needs and enhancing the Go1 platform’s governance and utility of data.
[Meet Morgan - Go1’s intelligent agent that brings learning into everyday work](https://www.go1.com/product/morgan)
![Image 4](https://go1-com.cdn.prismic.io/go1-com/Z_ZRuHdAxsiBwesm_Maskgroup.svg?fit=max&w=96)
![Image 5](https://go1-com.cdn.prismic.io/go1-com/Z_ZRtndAxsiBwesj_Maskgroup-1.svg?fit=max&w=128)
![Image 6](https://go1-com.cdn.prismic.io/go1-com/Z-vpUHdAxsiBwLay_Maskgroup-25.svg?fit=max&w=384)

“When people think about music, they often think of Spotify and access to unlimited music for one subscription. We believe Go1 is the emerging category leader in providing a similar experience for corporate learning. Powered by AI and machine learning, Go1’s platform provides an intuitive experience, and creates an opportunity for individuals to expand their professional development goals and explore the resources to help achieve them,” said Nagraj Kashyap, managing partner at SoftBank Investment Advisers, in a statement.

[Go1](https://www.go1.com/en-gb/), which provides curated online learning materials and tools to businesses using “playlists” that tap content from multiple publishers and silos, has closed a round of $200 million, a Series D that the Australian company’s CEO and co-founder Andrew Barnes confirmed values the startup at over $1 billion.

Barnes added that the funding will be used to expand further in existing markets. Based out of Brisbane, Australia, Go1 has offices in London, the U.S., Singapore and Malaysia, so it wants to go deeper into Europe more broadly and into more of Asia Pacific, he said. Go1 will also continue expanding its suite of services in the wider areas of learning and development training, he added.

Borrowing another media comparison, Barnes notes that he sees Go1 as occupying the “Netflix” button on a remote: regardless of the manufacturer or pay-TV provider, you still have a way to get your Netflix fix; and so, too, is the hope for Go1 in corporate learning and development training.

In 2025, the self-paced segment accounted for the major market share around 63%, driven by its flexibility, accessibility, and ability to cater to diverse learning schedules. The growing integration of AI-driven adaptive learning platforms and microlearning modules further enhances engagement in this segment.

The multimedia content dominates and holds the largest global e-learning market share in 2025. Multimedia content in e-learning encompasses educational materials that integrate diverse media formats such as text, audio, video, animations, and interactive visuals. This approach enhances engagement by stimulating multiple senses and creating an immersive learning environment. Multimedia content includes instructional videos, animated tutorials, podcasts, infographics, and interactive simulations that simplify complex concepts and maintain learner interest. By combining visual and auditory elements, it supports varied learning styles such as visual, auditory, and kinesthetic - making education more inclusive and impactful. Platforms such as Coursera, and edX effectively use multimedia content to promote deeper understanding, improve knowledge retention, and deliver high-quality, interactive learning experiences

Go1's platform serves employers looking to retain and upskill their talent and employees seeking training for professional and personal development.
Go1 has successfully expanded into the US and other global markets.
Go1 is recognized as a go-to provider of learning content for companies to upskill, reskill, and empower their workforces.
Go1 achieved a valuation of $US2.4 billion ($3.5 billion) in May 2023.

raw_passages.text: “Go1 has built a platform that serves the needs of both employers looking to retain and upskill their talent and employees seeking training for their professional and personal development,” said S.Somasegar, Managing Director, Madrona. “Go1’s successful expansion into the US and other global markets means they not only serve global corporations but are uniquely suited for the far flung remote workforces of the next decade. We are excited to work with the team on the next phase of growth.”

“Leading organizations are recognizing the acute need to future-proof their workforces by providing comprehensive learning and development opportunities,” said Andrew Barnes, CEO of Go1. “The incredible team at Go1 has made huge strides in expanding our capabilities and offerings to ensure users have access to education that supports their growth. These recent investments allow Go1 to build on that momentum to explore new content and resources, enabling our platform to meet the needs of every organization and employee, and brings us closer to our goal of supporting one billion learners globally.”

“Companies are embracing the opportunity to programmatically upskill, reskill and empower their workforces, and Go1 has emerged as the go-to provider of learning content to make that opportunity a reality,” said Craig Blair, Founder at AirTree Ventures. “We’re delighted to be a part of Go1’s global journey in building an enduring company at the helm of the Learning & Development ecosystem.”

●**Antony Ugoni, Chief Data Officer.** Ugoni has held a variety of senior leadership positions in data and analytics and is currently Chairperson on the advisory board for the Institute of Analytics Professionals of Australia. Ugoni will lead Go1’s data and data science teams, serving both internal business intelligence needs and enhancing the Go1 platform’s governance and utility of data.

However, as rates have peaked and started to decline in several key markets, and deposit behaviors have changed, net interest income is projected to grow more slowly, at about 2 percent per year through 2029, assuming no major disruptions. Meanwhile, growth in transaction-based revenue is expected to slow as consumers increasingly use lower-cost payment options like account-to-account transfers and digital wallets. At the same time, ongoing pricing pressures, especially within card-based ecosystems, combined with regulatory scrutiny and the rise of platform-driven payment experiences, are squeezing fee-based revenue models. Accordingly, we expect revenue growth to continue growing at 4 percent annually through 2029 (Exhibit 1). That number may range from as little as 3 percent in the case of global disruptions to as much as 6 percent with accelerated productivity improvements. At a growth rate of 4 percent, the total market size will reach $3.0 trillion by 2029.

Against this backdrop, the payments industry remains the most valuable part of financial services, generating $2.5 trillion in revenue from $2.0 quadrillion in value flows, supported by 3.6 trillion transactions worldwide.1 The _2025 McKinsey Global Payments Report_ offers insights into the future of the sector and what is needed to remain competitive in a rapidly changing environment. The report is based on analyses of McKinsey’s Global Payments Map, which includes data from 50 countries, more than two dozen payment methods, and accounts for 95 percent of global GDP. It is organized into three sections:

1.   A baseline forecast for industry growth through 2029, including a detailed examination of how economic volatility and policy changes are creating sharply divergent scenarios for margins and revenue mix.
2.   Major forces reshaping the payments landscape, including the monetization of AI-native operations and agentic commerce, new models of programmable liquidity, and regulated digital money.
3.   Investment priorities for operators navigating a transitioning system, focusing on agility, architecture, and trust.

From 2019 to 2024, global payments revenue increased on average by 7 percent annually. Interest income made up 46 percent of total revenues in 2024, supported by higher rates. In 2024, payments revenue growth slowed to 4 percent, a notable drop from the 12 percent increase in 2023. This deceleration was caused by peaking interest rates, a more muted macroeconomic environment, structural changes toward lower-yield payment methods, and ongoing fee pressures. Regionally, Latin America grew by 11 percent, while Europe, the Middle East, and Africa (EMEA) and North America increased by 8 percent and 5 percent, respectively, and Asia–Pacific (APAC) shrank by 1 percent. Nonetheless, payments is still the most valuable subsector in finance. In 2024, payments gave an average 18.9 percent return on equity, with some players earning more than 100 percent.2

A recognized thought leader and author, he speaks globally on the future of learning and partners with leaders to navigate disruption with clarity and confidence. His mission is to help organizations modernize learning in ways that create business value—and make work better for humans.

And why is this critical right now? The urgency and advantage gained by providing [AI training for employees](https://www.go1.com/blog/ai-training) will enable companies to secure a competitive edge in both productivity and employee retention.

Go1 helps L&D professionals launch and measure executive-driven initiatives with confidence. Our platform enables L&D to set strategy and co-create outcomes with learners, translating leadership vision into scalable, personalized learning experiences. Find more data from the learners' and L&D professionals' surveys in the _[Keeping Pace: Leading Learning in the Age of AI](https://www.go1.com/ai-with-go1)_ report.
L&D traditionally sits at the center of executive-driven learning strategies, which are mandated by leadership and then communicated to employees.

We surveyed over 2,000 L&D professionals and learners to understand how learner preferences and L&D strategies align or diverge in the era of AI. We examine the tension between self-directed and executive-driven approaches to see how L&D can bridge the gap between these two forces.

Premium Pro offers e-learning content sourced from over 250 content providers (including Go1's expanded Pro Library) and accessed via the Go1 platform and/or third-party integrations. The content library includes pre-curated learning pathways and on-demand search capabilities enabling admins and learners to discover relevant content based on specific terms, topics, and providers. Premium Pro customers also have the option to provide learners with access to Blinkist Enterprise.

Essentials Select provides access to the Go1 Premium Essentials library, offering flexible course selection tailored to each organization’s needs. Depending on the selected plan, customers can activate and use either 10, 25, or 50 courses at any given time, accessible through the Go1 platform or third-party integrations. Essentials Select admins can add Licensed Users to the account, assign specific e-learning courses, and monitor learning progress through reporting available on the Go1 platform (where applicable).

Access to Go1’s account team, including Customer Success Managers, is determined by your organisation’s size and spend. Your support tier will be communicated by Go1’s customer success team following execution of your Order Form. Outlined below are the support tiers and corresponding customer success services included with each.

Licensed User: is a single identified user on a named user basis, who is authorized by you to access Go1 e-learning content. The number of individual users accessing Go1 e-learning content under your Agreement may not exceed the number of Licensed Users set out in the Order Form (“Service Capacity”).

Go1 isn’t a traditional LMS—we’re a content platform designed to work seamlessly with your current tools. You can integrate Go1 into your LMS or HRIS for a streamlined experience, or use our platform as a lightweight solution for content management, consumption, and reporting. For organizations just getting started with L&D, Go1 can stand alone. For those with established systems, our robust integrations make managing content across platforms simple.

Learners can access Go1 through our mobile-optimized platform or directly within your existing systems using one of our 75+ integrations. Whether they’re logging in via your LMS, HRIS, or Go1 directly, the experience is consistent, intuitive, and built for ease of use.

We’ve designed Go1 to make online learning feel intuitive—not like another chore. That’s why we built **Go1 AI**: a new suite of features designed to simplify your workflow, save time, and bring more precision to your content decisions. Whether you’re building compliance programs, leadership tracks, or regional training plans, Go1 AI helps you find the right content faster and build more personalized learning journeys—without the manual lift.
![Image 2: Go1 AI Advanced Search](https://images.prismic.io/go1-com/aB4BQSdWJ-7kR1N__f980f425-0a22-4b23-a0db-6e6d4bdbb79c_Advanced%2BSearch.avif?auto=format,compress)

Traditional keyword search tools can miss the mark. With **AI-enhanced search**, Go1 AI understands the intent behind your queries—suggesting contextually relevant content and skills in seconds, not hours. It maps your needs to Go1’s extensive content library with deeper relevance and fewer clicks.
![Image 1: Go1 AI Chat](https://images.prismic.io/go1-com/aB4BgSdWJ-7kR1Oc_261900db-b6e1-483f-af39-b5d3f8d77427_AI%2BChat.avif?auto=format,compress)

Accordingly, AI isn’t infallible. It can be as helpful or biased as the data it’s fed. This is why we trained Go1 AI on the world’s largest and most diverse learning dataset**,**utilizing information from 156 million yearly course completions, encompassing 130,000 data points from 250+ content providers in 48 languages. This way, you have peace of mind that Go1 AI’s recommendations are relevant and timely.

Now, Go1 AI streamlines the curation process. L&D admins can generate personalized playlists based on their unique goals in seconds, making it highly scalable. Instead of manually creating playlists, Go1 AI searches our library of over 80,000 courses and curates relevant, personalized playlists in just a few clicks. Simply enter your learning goals, refine your parameters, and let Go1 AI do the rest.

As Holger Seim, Chief Product Officer at Go1,put it, "h _aving a vast library of learning content isn’t enough to engage learners in the workplace. L&D leaders need to surface the right content at the right time for each learner to achieve the best outcomes. By leveraging the wealth of data within our content library, Go1 is in the best position to provide smarter recommendations to L&D departments so they can build the most personalized and effective learning programs for their people."_

What does this mean for admins? Simple: this vast map of skills is interlinked, meaning Go1 AI is constantly learning what skills and courses relate to each other. Go1 AI can break down learning concepts into skills and sub-skills, recognizing links between closely matched skills and recommending associated content, thereby predicting future learning needs. We hope you’re nerding out as much as we are over this!

Microsoft | Go1
===============
[Meet Morgan - Go1’s intelligent agent that brings learning into everyday work](https://www.go1.com/product/morgan)
[English](https://www.go1.com/en/integrations/microsoft)[Français](https://www.go1.com/fr/en/integrations/microsoft)[Deutsch](https://www.go1.com/de/schulungsinhalte)

*   **Streamlined content management:** Easily import, update, and deactivate learning content from the Go1 catalog directly into the Workday ecosystem.
*   **Instant learner progress tracking**: Workday uses xAPI and webhook technology for real-time tracking, offering immediate insights into learner engagement and compliance.
*   **Enhanced learning experiences:** Merge [Go1's vast content library](https://www.go1.com/product/content-aggregator) with Workday to deliver personalized learning experiences that fuel continuous development.

The integration uses a sync of an employee’s curated catalog from the Go1 library, making it easy to import into the Workday ecosystem. Then, customers can complete their curation and synchronize their selections with just a few clicks. Once synchronized, the Workday integration retrieves course metadata and dynamically creates, updates, or deactivates content in the customer's Workday tenant to align with their latest selections.

Implementing this integration can be seamless and hassle-free. Prior to your first use, your Customer Success Manager (CSM) will raise a service request with the Go1 implementations team, who will configure and activate the integration. This should take no more than 24 hours. Following this, for customers with an existing Cloud Connect subscription, simply enter your OAuth client credentials from the Go1 portal to log in. From there, mapping options are available to tailor the integration to your organizational needs, ensuring a customized, uniform learning experience for all users.

Our partnership with Workday represents a commitment to providing best-in-class learning experiences tailored to the needs of modern organizations. By seamlessly combining Go1's comprehensive content library with Workday's robust ecosystem, customers can unlock new possibilities for employee development and growth.

The Go1 API lets you build apps and integrations on top of our content library and learning platform. Businesses use our API to deliver learning content within their platform, publish new content to the Go1 library, and to support a variety of learning experiences.
For more detailed information on our API versioning systems, please refer to our [API Versioning](https://developers.go1.com/docs/developer-tools/api/versioning/) documentation.

How Go1 hit $94.8M revenue and 3K customers in 2024.
====================================================

GO1.com is a learning platform that provides a wide range of courses to businesses and individuals. The platform offers access to thousands of courses from various providers and covers topics such as compliance, professional development, and personal interest. GO1.com aims to make learning easy and accessible for everyone, with features like personalized learning paths, team management tools, and integration with popular learning management systems. The company was founded in 2015 and is headquartered in Brisbane, Australia, with offices in the United States, United Kingdom, South Africa, Vietnam, and Malaysia.

In 2024, Go1’s revenue reached $94.8M up from $68.9M in 2023. The company previously reported $68.9M in 2023, $62.9M in 2022, $62.9M in 2022, $43.3M in 2021, $23.8M in 2020. Since its launch in 2009, Go1 has shown consistent revenue growth, reflecting its expanding user base and increasing adoption across various industries.

“Companies are embracing the opportunity to programmatically upskill, reskill and empower their workforces, and Go1 has emerged as the go-to provider of learning content to make that opportunity a reality,” said Craig Blair, Founder at AirTree Ventures. “We’re delighted to be a part of Go1’s global journey in building an enduring company at the helm of the Learning & Development ecosystem.”

“Go1 has built a platform that serves the needs of both employers looking to retain and upskill their talent and employees seeking training for their professional and personal development,” said S.Somasegar, Managing Director, Madrona. “Go1’s successful expansion into the US and other global markets means they not only serve global corporations but are uniquely suited for the far flung remote workforces of the next decade. We are excited to work with the team on the next phase of growth.”

“Leading organizations are recognizing the acute need to future-proof their workforces by providing comprehensive learning and development opportunities,” said Andrew Barnes, CEO of Go1. “The incredible team at Go1 has made huge strides in expanding our capabilities and offerings to ensure users have access to education that supports their growth. These recent investments allow Go1 to build on that momentum to explore new content and resources, enabling our platform to meet the needs of every organization and employee, and brings us closer to our goal of supporting one billion learners globally.”

●**Antony Ugoni, Chief Data Officer.** Ugoni has held a variety of senior leadership positions in data and analytics and is currently Chairperson on the advisory board for the Institute of Analytics Professionals of Australia. Ugoni will lead Go1’s data and data science teams, serving both internal business intelligence needs and enhancing the Go1 platform’s governance and utility of data.

[Go1](https://www.go1.com/en-gb/), which provides curated online learning materials and tools to businesses using “playlists” that tap content from multiple publishers and silos, has closed a round of $200 million, a Series D that the Australian company’s CEO and co-founder Andrew Barnes confirmed values the startup at over $1 billion.

Table of contents All Collections I access Go1 through my HRIS/LMS Integrating with Go1 via a partner Integrating Go1 Portals with Workday Integrating Go1 Portals with Workday Updated over 3 months ago Table of contents Background The CCL integration enables customers to import and track all their Go1 content easily and efficiently into their Workday tenant. Through the integration, customers can seamlessly and confidently be assured that their curated content selection is available and maintained and enrolment activity is captured and reported in their Workday environment. Completion events will be processed and recorded in Workday Learning in near real-time regardless of where the learner discovered or consumed the content.

​ ​ Pre-requisite Configurations in Workday Ensure the below steps have been completed: Learning module is configured in their Workday Tenant: https://doc.workday.com/admin-guide/en-us/human-capital-management/learning/learning-setup-and-maintenance/xof1593437444936.html?toc=9.0.0 Integration Systems User (ISU) is created: https://doc.workday.com/admin-guide/en-us/human-capital-management/learning/learning-content/cloud-connect-for-learning/fey1646155264903.html Security roles and permissions are added for the ISU user into the pre-existing ISSG_Cloud_Connect_For_Learning Security Group, or create a new user-based security group called Learning Administrator with the following permissions: View and Modify: Manage: Learning Content Manage: Learning Course Enrollments Manage: Learning Additional Data Person Data: Learning Reports: Learning Record Set Up: Learning Catalog Set Up: External Content Set Up: Learning External Content Integrations Cloud Connect for Learning Service Get and Put: Set Up: Learning External Content Integrations Set Up: External Content Cloud Connect for Learning Service Workday reference: https://doc.workday.com/admin-guide/en-us/human-capital-management/learning/learning-setup-and-maintenance/learning-security/jic1565173279687.html?toc=9.0.15.8 ​ ​ Configuration of CCL for your Content Provider - Customer Steps Note: These steps should be performed by a user with Learning Administrator permissions Search for Configure Cloud Connect for Learning in the global search bar at the top of any screen in your tenant.

You’ll be directed to the next task in the flow: Manage Cloud Connect for Learning Credentials. ​ ​ Enable the Generate Credentials button and click Next. You’ll be directed to the Generate Cloud Connect for Learning Credentials screen. On this screen, you’ll see the following (take note of these): Client ID Client Secret /auth url /tracking url /content url Select the Confirm check box and click Next to display the Conclusion screen. Click OK to complete the flow. Finally, share the acquired credentials from the above steps with your Go1 Customer Success Manager, who will help complete the required configuration in Go1. ​ ​ Using the integration and Trouble shooting To sync content from your Go1 portal, simply: Login to your Go1 portal as an admin and navigate to Go1 Admin. Simply select content to add to the Library using the Search experience Once add to your library, the content will be pushed to your Workday environment!

Note it may take a few hours for the content to be indexed into your Workday library after adding it in Go1. ​ Workday Troubleshooting For further assistance, contact Workday’s customer support . You must register as a Workday member to receive technical support. ​ ​ Questions If you have any configuration questions in Go1, please reach out to your dedicated Customer Success Manager. Through the integration, customers can seamlessly and confidently be assured that their curated content selection is available and maintained and enrolment activity is captured and reported in their Workday environment. Completion events will be processed and recorded in Workday Learning in near real-time regardless of where the learner discovered or consumed the content. Configuration steps in Go1 The following steps outline the Workday and Go1 CCL integration activation process. Step 1.

Provision API Keys For Workday to sync Go1 content, you must provision API keys in the Go1 portal. To complete this, simply follow the steps outlined in this guide , or speak to your dedicated Customer Success Manager who will arrange for this to be completed for you (The Go1 Implementation team can do this for you with the below step). Step 2. Configure the xAPI activity Tracker. Please follow the steps provided on the Workday Community site to generate the necessary xAPI credentials: https://community.workday.com/node/1171474 (see step 5 below). The Go1 Implementation team will support you in activating the xAPI activity tracker. Simply share the information acquired in the mentioned steps (step 6 below) with your Customer Success Manager, who will raise a request with the Go1 Implementation team to have this activated. Configuration steps in Workday Several steps in Workday must be completed before activating the Go1 learning provider in Workday.

As these steps are completed in Workday, please refer to the Workday support team and artefacts for any additional support required. The following steps are required to configure the Go1 learning provider in Workday: Set Up Cloud Connect for Learning Please follow the steps provided on the Workday Community Site under " Steps: Set Up Cloud Connect for Learning ": Once you can visit the “Configure External Content Provider” task, you have completed the necessary setup work. To configure the Go1 Learning Provider in Workday, take the following steps: From the "Configure External Content Provider" task in Workday, add a new external provider and choose "Go1". In the setup screen, paste in your Client Secret and Client ID , generated in Go1 . From the task, “Configure External Content”, map the Go1content to topics in Workday.

Specify a default topic that you can use for all content without a specified topic (you can do a linear mapping between Go1 topics and you Workday topics or something completely custom). To view the progress of the course content import, view the Process Monitor . The import takes a varying amount of time depending on the number of courses you choose to import. Run the Configure External Content Tracking Credentials task, select Go1 as the content provider and generate the xAPI credentials. Make a note of the client secret, client ID and other credentials. Share the credentials with Go1. The Go1 Implementation team will support you in activating the xAPI activity tracker i.e. the tracking integration. Run the Create Client Credentials Mapping task and enter the Workday Client ID and Integration System User. Login to your administrator Go1 portal and navigate to Content via your initials in the right-hand corner.

raw_passages.text: Online education continues to get a lot of attention in the wake of COVID-19 and the shift it brought to how people can learn. And to underscore that fact, Go1 — one of the rising stars in the world of enterprise learning, providing education and training to businesses in turn to offer to its employees or users — is announcing a significant round of $100 million, at over a $2 billion valuation, to fuel its growth. The funding — which closed in May — is being co-led by AirTree Ventures and Five Sigma, with SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Salesforce Ventures, Blue Cloud Ventures, Larsen Ventures, Scott Shleifer and John Curtius from Tiger Global, TEN13, M12 (Microsoft’s venture fund), Madrona Venture Group, SEEK and Y Combinator also participating. (The company was part of a Y Combinator cohort in 2015.) For some context on that valuation, Brisbane, Australia-based Go1 has now raised $400 million to date.

Go1 aggregates and curates the content, the idea being that its customers — which include companies that range from the likes of TikTok through to the Singaporean government — can ink a deal to be able to access that educational and training content without having to ink all of those agreements themselves. At a time when there is a lot of fragmentation and many options for e-learning, that approach has seen a lot of traction, largely to fill needs in three categories: training, upskilling and more general education to attract and retain talent. In the last year, CEO and co-founder Andrew Barnes told me in an interview that Go1’s revenues, customers and learners all doubled, and it now has some 5 million learners taking courses through its platform. And while most of its growth to date has been organic, it will be using some of the funding potentially to bring some inorganic growth into the mix.

Boston, MA | June 23, 2026 REGISTER NOW But Go1’s ambitions extend beyond that: It also plans to use some of the funding to further explore how it might extend its platform beyond corporate learning as well. “Right now our learners come to us through their employers, but we want to have a relationship outside of that context,” Barnes said. That is dovetailing with another ambition, he added. “Internally, we are considering how to provide education to everyone without pricing them out. If we do something in consumer, we would want to make that a target. It would be quite a different product.” Another area where it would like to use investment is to bring more technological innovations into the Go1 platform.

“We’re delighted to be a part of Go1’s global journey in building an enduring company at the helm of the Learning & Development ecosystem.” Similar to others in the same space such as Odilo (which announced funding just last week), Go1 positions itself as a kind of Netflix or Spotify, aggregating and curating content for its customers. Unlike Odilo, Go1 keeps its branding intact throughout the experience, more like a YouTube. Barnes said there are no plans to move into a completely white-label product.

GO1.com is a learning platform that provides a wide range of courses to businesses and individuals. The platform offers access to thousands of courses from various providers and covers topics such as compliance, professional development, and personal interest. GO1.com aims to make learning easy and accessible for everyone, with features like personalized learning paths, team management tools, and integration with popular learning management systems. The company was founded in 2015 and is headquartered in Brisbane, Australia, with offices in the United States, United Kingdom, South Africa, Vietnam, and Malaysia.

In 2024, Go1’s revenue reached $94.8M up from $68.9M in 2023. The company previously reported $68.9M in 2023, $62.9M in 2022, $62.9M in 2022, $43.3M in 2021, $23.8M in 2020. Since its launch in 2009, Go1 has shown consistent revenue growth, reflecting its expanding user base and increasing adoption across various industries.

In this debut edition, we’ll shine a spotlight on compliance and retention courses, before sharing the best new and returning content providers in the Go1 Library. So, what’s trending in learning this March?

Every month, we’ll focus on a different L&D topic, recommending associated courses from the Go1 library. To kick things off, it’s a big one: compliance and retention. While we probably don’t need to tell you how important these topics are (_very!),_ a quick reminder couldn’t hurt: [87% percent](https://blog.capterra.com/upskilling-employees-research/) of HR leaders say their employee L&D[](https://www.workramp.com/blog/what-is-learning-and-development/)program is critical to retaining talent.

**Course description:**How does a company become a champion of retention? This course deconstructs the misconceptions surrounding retention and provides the key to understanding the new habits of the labor market. It raises the question of the role of managers and human resources and lists good practices for retaining employees by remaining flexible and arming yourself with the right tools to enhance each person's skills.

### **For more insights, subscribe to the Go1 newsletter to stay on top of all the latest L&D trends. Or, [book a demo today to find](https://www.go1.com/speak-to-an-expert)out how Go1 can help with your team’s learning needs.**
Traditional training, often conducted through [legacy systems](https://www.go1.com/blog/identify-and-overcome-legacy-systems-in-employee-training), can:

*   **Cause cognitive overload:** Learners retain less when sessions drag on. A typical ["forgetting curve"](https://www.go1.com/blog/overcome-the-forgetting-curve-in-corporate-training)hypothesizes that participants tend to forget more than [50% of their newly learned](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6716752/)material 20 minutes immediately after the lesson ends. *   **Take up too much time:** Corporate learners are busy and can typically only devote [24 minutes to learning per week.](https://joshbersin.com/2018/06/a-new-paradigm-for-corporate-training-learning-in-the-flow-of-work/#_ftnref6)
*   **Decrease completion rates:**Some studies show that, on average, [online course dropout rates are as high as 96%.](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/330316898_The_MOOC_pivot) Long training often only exacerbates this. *   **Diminish productivity:** Long trainings, which can be mentally taxing, can make employees less productive when it comes to their actual work.
*   **Cost more money:**Higher development costs, more time away from productive work, and poor retention rates reduce ROI compared to shorter training formats.
By focusing on frequency and relevance over duration, you can cut training time in half while actually improving retention and application.

Go1's analytics platform provides measurement capabilities to track engagement, retention, and real-world application of learning.
Go1's platform can track sustained engagement with content beyond initial requirements and retention of knowledge weeks and months later.
Go1's Skills Insights feature tracks the skills employees are developing through learning activity, providing a data-driven view of top skills and learning engagement.
Go1 automatically tags all content with up to seven skills, and when an employee engages with content, those skills are tracked to generate insights.
Admins can view each learner’s individual quiz attempts, which is useful for tracking assessment performance and improvement.
Go1's platform supports spaced learning approaches like microlearning modules, periodic quizzes, and refresher content to provide measurable retention data.
The platform can automate the reinforcement process by delivering targeted review content and follow-up assessments to track knowledge persistence.
Learner reports in Go1 show summary information for each learner, including progress metrics across statuses like Not Started, In Progress, and Completed.
Go1's platform can track observable changes in workplace behavior and improvement in work output and performance as learning outcomes.

raw_passages.text: A customer value framework is a structured process that can help you pinpoint your value proposition by considering the relevant factors and elements that influence how valuable your customers see your product. While you can find many different suggestions for which framework to follow, three key elements of a value proposition are understanding who your customer is, how you’re different from your competitors, and how relevant and important your product is to customers. A customer value proposition framework gives you a methodological approach to determining your value proposition and offers solutions for integrated frameworks, such as [Agile](https://www.coursera.org/articles/what-is-agile-a-beginners-guide), that can help you manage feedback and continuous improvement.

A value proposition serves as both a mission statement and a [marketing](https://www.coursera.org/articles/marketing-strategy) tool; it describes what the company, product, or service does. Before starting your business, it’s important to create an effective value proposition to differentiate yourself from others. It also illustrates what makes the company’s offering superior to its competitors.

Having a unique value proposition creates company value for its customers. For example, until wireless headphones came along, customers didn’t realize they wanted headphones. It helps a company of any size attract investors, new customers, or clients. It can also help keep customers and boost [brand loyalty](https://www.coursera.org/articles/brand-loyalty).

We count the total number of Paid Enterprise Customers that are active on our platform at the end of each period. For purposes of determining our customer count, we treat each customer account that has a corresponding contract as a unique customer, and a single organization with multiple divisions, segments, or subsidiaries may be counted as multiple customers. We define a “Paid Enterprise Customer” as a customer who purchases Coursera via our direct sales force. For purposes of determining our Paid Enterprise Customer count, we exclude our Enterprise customers who do not purchase Coursera via our direct sales force, including organizations engaging on our platform through our Coursera for Teams offering or through our channel partners.

We calculate annual recurring revenue (“ARR”) by annualizing each customer’s monthly recurring revenue (“MRR”) for the most recent month at period end. We calculate “Net Retention Rate” for a period by starting with the ARR from all Paid Enterprise Customers as of the 12 months prior to such period end, or Prior Period ARR. We then calculate the ARR from these same Paid Enterprise Customers as of the current period end, or “Current Period ARR”. Current Period ARR includes expansion within Paid Enterprise Customers and is net of contraction or attrition over the trailing 12 months but excludes revenue from new Paid Enterprise Customers in the current period. We then divide the total Current Period ARR by the total Prior Period ARR to arrive at our Net Retention Rate for Paid Enterprise Customers.

Our latest case study profiles Coursera, an online education company whose mission is to provide anyone, anywhere with life-changing access to some of the world’s best higher education. An IFC client since 2013, Coursera uses technology to help students overcome access barriers like high tuition costs and lack of availability of desired courses in their region. Coursera was launched in 2012 by Andrew Ng and Daphne Koller with a mission to provide universal access to world-class learning. It is now one of the largest online learning platforms in the world, with 175 million registered learners as of March 31, 2025. Coursera partners with over 350 leading university and industry leaders to offer a broad catalog of content and credentials, including courses, Specializations, Professional Certificates, and degrees. Coursera’s platform innovations enable instructors to deliver scalable, personalized, and verified learning experiences to their learners. Institutions worldwide rely on Coursera to upskill and reskill their employees, citizens, and students in high-demand fields, including GenAI, data science, technology, and business. Coursera is a Delaware public benefit corporation and a B Corp.

Coursera, a leading online learning platform, has been named to the fifth annual [TIME100 Most Influential Companies](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Ftime.com%2Fcollections%2Ftime100-companies-2025%2F7289605%2Fcoursera%2F&esheet=54284484&newsitemid=20250701166802&lan=en-US&anchor=TIME100+Most+Influential+Companies&index=1&md5=04838cbfa643b5d431874f5c2be9e22a) list, which highlights companies making an extraordinary impact around the world.

“Generative AI presents both a unique challenge and an exciting opportunity to the global workforce,” said Greg Hart, CEO of Coursera. “Being named one of the most influential companies by _Time_ is a tremendous honor—and a reminder of the responsibility we share with our partners to keep expanding access to high-demand skills for learners around the world.”

With GenAI transforming the labor market, it is also driving a significant shift in online education as people seek to learn how to understand and apply this new technology. Coursera earned its place on the TIME100 list for its relentless work towards democratizing access to AI education. The company offers more than 750 GenAI courses from leading universities and companies such Google, IBM, DeepLearning.AI, Vanderbilt University, the University of Michigan, and the University of Pennsylvania, and the surge in demand continues to rise. This year, Coursera has seen 12 enrollments per minute in GenAI content on the platform.

I’m delighted to present Coursera’s [sixth annual _Global Skills Report_](https://www.coursera.org/skills-reports/global/), a trusted resource for leaders and institutions worldwide to understand the rapidly transforming skills landscape. The report draws on data and insights from our global learning community—including over 148 million learners and 7,000 institutional customers—and content from 325 of the world’s leading university and industry partners. To provide a holistic view, the report now combines our internal proficiency data with leading economic indices, including [global innovation](https://www.wipo.int/global_innovation_index/en/), [labor force participation](https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/SL.TLF.CACT.ZS), [human capital](https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/HD.HCI.OVRL), and [GDP per capita](https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/NY.GDP.PCAP.CD).

*   **Nearly one-third of US workers lack foundational digital skills, with workers of color disproportionately affected.** As the public and private sectors digitize, the need for highly trained STEM workers grows. However, fewer than 100,000 US graduates earning engineering and computer science degrees each year. 
    *   The 1,058% surge in GenAI course enrollments and the 61% year-over-year growth in Professional Certificate enrollments among American learners demonstrate the country’s commitment to closing this digital skills gap and preparing for the digital economy.
    *   Washington is the United States’ most skilled state, achieving the country’s highest proficiency scores for _Technology_ and _Data Science._ It is followed by Colorado and Michigan.

The report captures several significant trends driven by GenAI, digital transformation, and automation. In 2023, a learner signed up for a GenAI course on Coursera every minute. By 2024, this rate had quadrupled. A **1,060% year-over-year**increase in global GenAI course enrollments highlights how learners are actively preparing for AI’s impact on their careers.

*   **European learners on the Coursera platform record the highest skills proficiency levels.**19 of the top 25 countries globally are from the region, with Switzerland emerging as a global skills leader. *   In contrast, **major Anglophone nations like**New Zealand (40th), the United Kingdom (45th), Australia (55th), Canada (59th), and the United States (69th) rank lower. *   **Japanese learners are the most proficient in Asia-Pacific**, with Japan having risen from 5th to 2nd in the global ranking. It is the only APAC nation to feature among the top ten. Singapore has risen from 16th to 12th, while India ranks 87th
    *   **Latin America’s highest-ranked nation is Brazil (19th)**, with Chile (20th) also among the top 20. Latin America and the Caribbean show a strong commitment to AI readiness, with GenAI course enrollment increasing 882% year-over-year.

raw_passages.text: ### Coursera Partners with OpenAI to Bring Learning Capabilities into the First Generation of Apps in ChatGPT

Coursera (NYSE: COUR), a leading global online learning platform, today announced it is one of OpenAI’s first generation of apps in ChatGPT, unveiled at OpenAI’s DevDay. This partnership marks the first time an online learning platform has been directly embedded in ChatGPT — making trusted, world-class educational content more accessible to hundreds of millions of learners worldwide.

Every week, more than 800 million people use ChatGPT, with one of the most common use cases being learning. Now, these users will be able to access relevant Coursera videos and information in ChatGPT conversations, making educational content more discoverable and turning everyday chats into dynamic, interactive learning experiences. To access the Coursera app in ChatGPT, users can ask ChatGPT for the app by name. ChatGPT will also suggest when it recognizes that Coursera content may be useful to the conversation.

“This partnership reflects Coursera and OpenAI’s shared commitment to expanding access to education and helping people everywhere learn, grow, and thrive,” said Greg Hart, CEO of Coursera. “By putting trusted, verified learning into the hands of hundreds of millions of people, we can help them gain the skills they need to pursue economic opportunity and prepare for the jobs of tomorrow.”

What Is Coursera? Written by Coursera Staff • Updated on Jul 28, 2025 Coursera is a global online learning platform that offers anyone, anywhere, access to online courses and degrees from leading universities and companies. Coursera is an online learning platform featuring many different subjects across an array of learning formats, such as courses, Specializations, Professional Certificates, degrees, and tutorials. Over 300 leading universities and companies, including Stanford, Duke, Illinois, the University of Colorado Boulder, Google, IBM, Microsoft, and Meta, provide instruction on Coursera. Whether you're looking to develop a new skill, strengthen an existing one, further your learning with a formal credential like a Professional Certificate or degree, or just learn something for fun, Coursera has many options to choose from. How does Coursera work?

Much of the learning you'll encounter on Coursera takes place asynchronously , meaning you can access course content and materials at your own pace. That way, you can build your learning into your schedule and around your other responsibilities. Coursera prioritizes top-quality learning through evidence-based online teaching and learning strategies. The average rating across courses on the Coursera platform is 4.7 out of 5 stars, with 73 percent of learners who complete courses reporting positive career-related outcomes. You can learn more about our methods and data in our research analysis, Drivers of Quality in Online Learning . What is Coursera Plus? Coursera Plus is a subscription available in either monthly or annual tiers that gives you access to over 10,000 courses on Coursera, including those from Google, Microsoft, and IBM. Build job-ready skills with Coursera Plus Start 7-day free trial Start 7-day free trial Is Coursera worth it?

You can start learning on Coursera either by taking a class or by auditing a class. This means that you can begin learning new skills today. If you decide that you want to pursue the credential that comes with the class, you can upgrade at any time. Types of learning on Coursera From tech, engineering, and business to the arts, humanities, and social sciences, there are all kinds of subjects to learn on Coursera. Let's review the different types of learning you'll find on the platform. What is a Coursera certificate? Coursera certificates are credentials that prove you’ve successfully completed a course or program. They are secure URLs stored on the Accomplishments page of your Coursera account. You can share them online, post them to your LinkedIn, or download them as a PDF file to print. Each Coursera certificate includes the course name, instructor’s signature, and the logo of any affiliated partner institution.

Confirmation that Coursera has verified your identity will also be included alongside a verification URL you can share with employers or anyone who may want to check the authenticity of your certificate. What is a Professional Certificate on Coursera? Professional Certificates are designed to focus on job-ready skills, making them an excellent choice for those starting a new career or advancing in their current one. They are training programs led by industry leaders such as Google, IBM, Meta, Salesforce, Microsoft, and CVS. Upon completion of the program, you’ll earn a Professional Certificate from the offering institution confirming your successful completion of the training, which you can feature on your resume . You can browse Professional Certificate programs here . What is a Coursera Specialization? Similar to Professional Certificates, Specializations are course series centered around helping you master specific subject matter.

The online learning industry has seen exponential growth over the past decade, with platforms like Coursera leading the charge. But have you ever wondered how such platforms generate revenue while offering free courses to millions of users? This blog explores the success story of Coursera, delves into its business model, and explains how you can build a similar online learning platform with the help of Yo!Coach.

Overall, given that Coursera’s largest source of revenues is verified certificates, and with the current revenue rate of $1M per month, we estimate that Coursera is on its way to making $8-12 million in revenues in 2014. According to Coursera CEO Rick Levin, a [couple of universities](http://www.washingtonpost.com/local/education/new-coursera-chief-stresses-the-wow-factor-of-huge-audience-for-free-online-courses/2014/06/23/bf27a1fe-fad4-11e3-8176-f2c941cf35f1_story.html) are already recovering their costs through shared revenue. [Documents](https://www.documentcloud.org/documents/400864-coursera-fully-executed-agreement.html#document/p40) obtained by [The Chronicle of Higher Education](http://chronicle.com/article/How-an-Upstart-Company-Might/133065/) shows Coursera shares with universities 6-15% of the total revenue and 20% of gross profits on its courses.

Why have VCs invested so much money in the company? How does offering free online courses generate revenue? Many have asked, so we examined Coursera’s different monetization models and offer estimates based on some known numbers.

Coursera charged [companies a flat fee](http://chronicle.com/article/Providers-of-Free-MOOCs-Now/136117/) for introductions to matched students. The revenue would be shared with the university whose courses the student had registered for. At launch, positions were limited to Software Engineering and initial companies using the service included Facebook, Twitter, AppDirect, and TrialPay.

![Image 1](https://edsurge.imgix.net/uploads/photo/image/1358/2014-10-15-coursera-1-1413352709-1428753478-1428759066.jpg?w=216&h=108&auto=compress,format&fit=fill&bg=fff&pad=0&blur=10&px=4)
Nine months after the launch, Coursera had hit [$1 million in revenue](http://blog.coursera.org/post/61047298750/a-milestone-for-signature-track-certificates-for-the) through 25,000 sales of verified certificates among its 4.7 million students. Five months later, cumulative revenues reportedly reached [$4 million](http://donaldclarkplanb.blogspot.co.uk/2014/04/moocs-coursera-moves-towards-massive.html).

*   **The Pivot to Paid Credentials (2013-2015):** The initial model of free MOOCs was great for access but terrible for revenue. Introducing paid Specializations and Professional Certificates, especially with industry partners like Google and IBM, created a sustainable revenue stream and made the platform relevant for career advancement. This is where the business model truly took shape. *   **Expansion into Enterprise Learning (2015):** Launching Coursera for Business (now Coursera for Enterprise) was a game-changer. It diversified the customer base from individual consumers to large organizations, which pay higher, recurring fees to upskill their workforce. This segment is key to long-term stability and growth, and the company is still investing heavily here, like the recent appointment of Anthony Salcito as General Manager of Enterprise.

*   **Subscription Dominance:** The Consumer segment's growth is increasingly powered by the Coursera Plus subscription, which now accounts for more than half of the segment's revenue. This is a defintely positive trend, as subscriptions create a more stable, recurring revenue base. *   **Gross Margin Strength:** The platform maintains a strong overall Gross Margin, which was 56% in Q3 2025. The Enterprise segment has an even higher gross profit margin, sitting at around 70%, while the Consumer segment's gross margin is approximately 61%. *   **Strategic Pricing:** Pricing is variable: a single course certificate might cost $49, a Professional Certificate a few hundred dollars, and the Coursera Plus subscription is around $399 per year. This allows them to monetize casual learners, career-focused individuals, and institutions all at once. *   **AI-Driven Efficiency:** The company is strategically investing in AI-driven tools like Coursera Coach, which acts as a personalized tutor.

Coursera, Inc. is the definitive leader in the digital upskilling market, but do you defintely know how its dual-engine model-Consumer and Enterprise-is driving its financial reality? The company projects full-year 2025 revenue to land between **$750 million** and **$754 million**, a guidance raise fueled by a 13% year-over-year surge in its Consumer segment alone. With a massive base of 191 million registered learners as of Q3 2025, Coursera's mission to provide world-class learning is clearly resonating, but the real story is how its scale and AI-native features are translating into a sustainable business model and investment opportunity. You need to understand the mechanics behind this growth, from its university partnerships to its Generative AI strategy, to assess its long-term market value.

| Product/Service | Target Market | Key Features |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Consumer (Courses, Specializations, Professional Certificates, Coursera Plus) | Individual Learners (B2C) | Access to over **12,000 courses**; Job-ready Professional Certificates (e.g., Google, IBM); Coursera Plus subscription for unlimited access; Pay-per-course or subscription model. |
| Coursera for Business | Global Corporations and Small-to-Midsize Businesses (B2B) | Curated skill development content for employees; Enterprise-level analytics and skill tracking; Access to a catalog of over **100 Professional Certificates**. |
| Coursera for Government & Campus | Governments, Non-profits, and Universities (B2G/B2U) | Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) for citizens/students; Workforce recovery and upskilling programs; Integration into university curricula.

Before we get into the details, a quick reality check of just how big an opportunity there is, with real numbers. Coursera’s 2024 revenue was $694.7 million across three segments: Consumer, Enterprise, and Degrees. In Q2 2025, revenue reached [$187.1 million](https://s27.q4cdn.com/928340662/files/doc_financials/2024/ar/COUR_Financial-Statement_2024.pdf) with a small GAAP net loss and positive non-GAAP profitability. Scale is real, and demand continues to rise. Now let’s start from the beginning.

Coursera, a leading online learning platform, has been named to the fifth annual [TIME100 Most Influential Companies](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Ftime.com%2Fcollections%2Ftime100-companies-2025%2F7289605%2Fcoursera%2F&esheet=54284484&newsitemid=20250701166802&lan=en-US&anchor=TIME100+Most+Influential+Companies&index=1&md5=04838cbfa643b5d431874f5c2be9e22a) list, which highlights companies making an extraordinary impact around the world.

“Generative AI presents both a unique challenge and an exciting opportunity to the global workforce,” said Greg Hart, CEO of Coursera. “Being named one of the most influential companies by _Time_ is a tremendous honor—and a reminder of the responsibility we share with our partners to keep expanding access to high-demand skills for learners around the world.”

With GenAI transforming the labor market, it is also driving a significant shift in online education as people seek to learn how to understand and apply this new technology. Coursera earned its place on the TIME100 list for its relentless work towards democratizing access to AI education. The company offers more than 750 GenAI courses from leading universities and companies such Google, IBM, DeepLearning.AI, Vanderbilt University, the University of Michigan, and the University of Pennsylvania, and the surge in demand continues to rise. This year, Coursera has seen 12 enrollments per minute in GenAI content on the platform.

In addition to its vast content catalog, Coursera has harnessed the power of AI to launch powerful features that increase access, including course translations in 26 languages and voice dubbing in six languages. Millions of learners worldwide can now develop job-relevant skills more effectively in their native language.

The report is based on analyses of McKinsey’s Global Payments Map, which includes data from 50 countries, more than two dozen payment methods, and accounts for 95 percent of global GDP. It is organized into three sections:

1.   A baseline forecast for industry growth through 2029, including a detailed examination of how economic volatility and policy changes are creating sharply divergent scenarios for margins and revenue mix.
2.   Major forces reshaping the payments landscape, including the monetization of AI-native operations and agentic commerce, new models of programmable liquidity, and regulated digital money.

From 2019 to 2024, global payments revenue increased on average by 7 percent annually. Interest income made up 46 percent of total revenues in 2024, supported by higher rates. In 2024, payments revenue growth slowed to 4 percent, a notable drop from the 12 percent increase in 2023. This deceleration was caused by peaking interest rates, a more muted macroeconomic environment, structural changes toward lower-yield payment methods, and ongoing fee pressures. Regionally, Latin America grew by 11 percent, while Europe, the Middle East, and Africa (EMEA) and North America increased by 8 percent and 5 percent, respectively, and Asia–Pacific (APAC) shrank by 1 percent. Nonetheless, payments is still the most valuable subsector in finance. In 2024, payments gave an average 18.9 percent return on equity, with some players earning more than 100 percent.2
